answer: Source of income discrimination is unlawful in New York City. When a landlord or broker refuses a voucher, says "no programs", or otherwise treats you differently because of source of income, you should report it. Please note that your report will be routed to a human on the openigloo team. You can also report denials to the NYC Commission on Human Rights immediately while the unit is still available.

answer: A listing marked "no fee" on openigloo means you will not pay a broker fee at any point: not when you apply, not when you sign, and not after you move in. If anyone asks you for a broker fee on a listing marked "no fee", do not pay it. Additionally, under New York City law, a landlord's agent or an agent who publishes a listing with the permission or authorization of the landlord shall not impose or collect any fee from a tenant related to the rental of such property.

answer: Under openigloo's policy, listings on openigloo may not request more than one month's rent as a security deposit in any building. Additionally, New York law caps the security deposit at one month's rent for all residential leases signed on or after June 14, 2019. Because a fee or deposit demand exceeding this limit violates openigloo's listing standards, this report will be routed to a human on the openigloo team who will follow up with you.

citations.section: P7. Security deposits on openigloo listings
citations.quote: Listings on openigloo may not request more than one month's rent as a security deposit, and may not request prepaid rent beyond the first month, in any building. This is openigloo's own listing standard and applies whether or not the law would allow more for a particular unit. If a renter reports being asked for more, the assistant quotes the legal cap, quotes this rule, and routes the report to a human.

New York law caps the security deposit at one month's rent for all residential leases signed on or after June 14, 2019. Landlords may not collect additional deposits, "key money", or prepaid last month's rent on top of that.

citations.section: P10. When to hand off to a human
citations.quote: The assistant routes the conversation to a human on the openigloo team when: a renter reports discrimination (P4); a renter reports a fee or deposit demand that violates openigloo's listing standards (P6, P7); a renter reports a lockout, utility shutoff or removal of belongings; a renter says they have received court papers; or the renter asks the same question three times without accepting the answer. The assistant tells the renter that a person will follow up and does not promise a time.

When reporting no hot water, the proper steps are to quote the legal requirement, file a complaint with 311, and keep a dated record of the condition.

answer: A discrimination report routed by the assistant goes to the trust queue with high priority. If two confirmed reports occur against the same landlord within 90 days, it results in the removal of all of that landlord's listings and a written notice sent to the landlord.
